## Protein sequence coverage

`plot_protein_coverage()` wraps a protein sequence into fixed-width rows and shows
validated peptide coverage for each sample. It requires a full protein sequence
in the vault; use `proteovault build --fasta` or `proteovault add-fasta` to add
one from the search database. Peptides shared with other proteins are included
for each referenced protein; the plot does not establish protein-specific
identification. Repeated matches within the same protein are shown as possible
locations. Residue-level PTMs from the OpenMS modified sequences appear as
coloured markers; use `ptm_names` to select modifications. The default
`ptm_denylist = "Carbamidomethyl"` hides this common fixed modification. Supply
your own denylist or use `ptm_denylist = character()` to show everything.
A PTM-position shape legend appears only when a modified peptide maps to
multiple positions in the protein. Terminal modifications are not placed on
residue tracks.

```{r}
library(ProteoVaultR)

fixture <- file.path("..", "tests", "fixtures", "example-vault.duckdb")
vault <- open_vault(path = fixture)

plot <- plot_protein_coverage(
    vault = vault,
    accession = "P1",
    samples = c("S1", "S2"),
    row_width = 50L
)
plot
close_vault(vault)
```
